agent_notes.bjorn: Completed tech stack selection (2026-03-30). Deliverable: output/2026-03-30-tech-stack.md. Decision: Next.js 15 App Router with output: 'export' (fully static), Tailwind CSS v4, Framer Motion, Lucide React, next-themes for dark mode, fontsource for self-hosted fonts, deploy to Vercel free tier. No decisions are hard to reverse at this stage. Arve should use placeholder images and text wordmark until Jorunn delivers brand assets. Accent color (#7C6FFF) wired as CSS variable for single-line swap pending Jorunn confirmation. | Completed authentication system architecture (2026-04-01). Deliverable: output/2026-04-01-authentication-system-architecture.md. Key decisions: stateless JWT (HS256, 24h expiry) over session cookies; bcrypt via passlib for password hashing; refresh tokens omitted at launch; owner_id FK on links uses ON DELETE SET NULL to preserve redirects; rate limiting 5 req/15min/IP via SlowAPI. Two hard-to-reverse flags: (1) stateless JWT means no instant token revocation without Redis blocklist later; (2) in-memory rate limiting fails under horizontal scaling. Auth endpoints should be prefixed /auth/ for namespacing. GET /auth/me and is_active field noted for arve. JWT_SECRET_KEY secret provisioning noted for dag.
agent_notes.else: Completed market & competitor research (2026-03-30). Deliverable: output/2026-03-30-market-research.md. Researched 8 direct competitors with live landing page data: Notion AI, Otter.ai, Reclaim.ai, Motion, Superhuman, Mem.ai, Reflect, Granola. Positioning gaps for Neutral: calm/anti-hustle tone, privacy-first, single-professional premium tier, augmentation vs. full-automation framing. Recommend Jorunn read the gaps section before writing brand copy. | Completed competitive analysis of AI agent platforms (2026-04-01). Deliverable: output/2026-04-01-competitive-analysis.md. Researched 8 platforms: Relevance AI, Lindy, Zapier, Make, n8n, CrewAI, Dust, AgentOps. Key finding: upper-left quadrant (high reasoning + non-technical interface) is least crowded — that is where AI Office should position. Three whitespace opportunities: (1) mid-market reasoning gap for ops leads without engineering teams, (2) transparent predictable pricing in a market where every competitor has credit confusion, (3) internal knowledge + reasoning combination (highest effort, most defensible). Flag: n8n adding AI pricing friction contradicts market trend toward AI-as-baseline. Lindy is SEO incumbent in self-serve; budget for content strategy if targeting that segment.

agent_notes.magnus: Completed privacy policy and GDPR/CCPA compliance work (2026-04-01). Deliverables: output/2026-04-01-privacy-policy.md and output/2026-04-01-compliance-checklist.md. Key decisions: (1) AI Office is controller for account data, processor for Customer Content; (2) Customer Content must NOT be used to train AI models without explicit written consent; (3) standard DPA must be published before accepting EEA customers; (4) DPIA required for AI agent processing before EEA launch; (5) 20 engineering launch blockers identified (consent flows, DSR API, audit logs, encryption, sub-processor DPAs). Both documents require qualified legal counsel review before publication. | Completed GDPR compliance analysis for user auth system (2026-04-01). Deliverable: output/2026-04-01-gdpr-compliance-user-auth.md. Key findings: (1) 7 categories of personal data collected including referrer/user-agent which require a Legitimate Interests Assessment before EEA launch; (2) Click cascade-delete works via existing SQLAlchemy rule BUT user->link cascade is missing and must be added before erasure works; (3) JWT statelessness creates 24-hour erasure gap after account deletion — team must decide on token blocklist vs reduced TTL; (4) POST /register leaks email enumeration via 409 response — security and GDPR risk; (5) 8 hard launch blockers identified including DELETE /me endpoint, Privacy Policy publication, ToS acceptance at registration, and LIA documentation; (6) email verification strongly recommended for data integrity.
agent_notes.nora: Completed B2B SaaS pricing model (2026-04-01). Deliverable: output/2026-04-01-pricing-model.md. Three tiers confirmed: Free ($0, 50 AI runs/mo, 500 notes), Pro ($12/mo annual, 1,000 runs/mo, unlimited notes, E2E encryption, 14-day trial no credit card), Team ($24/seat/mo annual, 5,000 runs/seat, SSO, admin controls, sales-assisted close). Modeled two scenarios: flat subscription (Scenario A, recommended at launch) and usage-based with monthly cap (Scenario B, recommended post-50 customers). Unit economics: Pro gross margin 85%, LTV:CAC 1.73x (target 3x within 12 months), payback 10.4 months. Team gross margin 91%, LTV:CAC 3.28x, payback 7.3 months. Revenue projections: $28K ARR at 100 customers, $174K at 500, $413K at 1,000. Key decisions: no credit card for Pro trial, Team tier minimum 3 seats sales-assisted only, do not raise Pro annual price before 200 paying customers.

agent_notes.dag: Completed auth infrastructure and secrets management (2026-04-01). Deliverables: (1) output/2026-04-01-docker-compose-auth.yml — adds JWT_SECRET_KEY, JWT_ALGORITHM, ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES, REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRE_DAYS, RATE_LIMIT_AUTH_LOGIN, RATE_LIMIT_AUTH_REGISTER env vars; (2) output/2026-04-01-env-example-auth — updated .env.example with all new vars and secure generation instructions; (3) output/2026-04-01-dockerfile-auth — adds libffi-dev to builder stage (required for cffi/python-jose), switches CMD to --workers 2 so Redis-backed rate limit counters are shared; (4) output/2026-04-01-github-actions-ci-auth.yml — adds 'alembic upgrade head' step before pytest in CI, adds Railway deploy job that runs alembic post-deploy via 'railway run'; (5) output/2026-04-01-rate-limiting-setup.py — drop-in app/rate_limiting.py using slowapi backed by Redis, configurable limits via env vars, structured 429 response; (6) output/2026-04-01-ops-readme-auth-section.md — JWT secret rotation procedure, Alembic migration workflow (CI and production), rate limit config, bcrypt concurrency warning. Key decisions: [DECISION] JWT_SECRET_KEY rotated via Railway env panel (immediate, no code change, invalidates all tokens) (2026-04-01). [DECISION] Alembic migrations run in CI against live Postgres service container to validate before push, and via 'railway run' after new image is live (additive-only schema changes required for zero-downtime) (2026-04-01). [DECISION] slowapi with Redis storage backend chosen over nginx rate limiting — simpler to configure, reversal is one env var change, Redis already in stack (2026-04-01). Bottleneck flag: bcrypt hashing is synchronous and blocks uvicorn workers at high concurrency — acceptable at launch, document threshold at 500 concurrent auth requests.
agent_notes.bjorn_md2html: Completed markdown-to-HTML converter CLI architecture (2026-04-07). Deliverable: output/2026-04-07-system-architecture.md. Key decisions: [DECISION] Python over Node.js — consistent with team stack, no second runtime required (2026-04-07). [DECISION] mistune 3.x as Markdown parser — pure Python, CommonMark-compliant, isolated behind parser.parse() interface for easy swap (2026-04-07). [DECISION] CSS embedded inline in output HTML — self-contained portable output, no external file dependency (2026-04-07). [DECISION] watchdog in optional extras (pip install md2html[watch]) — avoids C extension in base install (2026-04-07). Stack: Python 3.11+, mistune 3.x, Jinja2 3.x, click 8.x, watchdog 4.x (optional). Module breakdown: cli.py, reader.py, parser.py, renderer.py, writer.py, watcher.py, themes/. CLI flags: --input, --output, --theme, --watch. No database, no server, no Docker required.
